secret.title: Webhook secret
secret.outboundTitle: Signing secret of the calls it sends
secret.howtoOutbound: Paste it in the receiving service: every call carries webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature (Standard Webhooks, HMAC-SHA256 of "id.timestamp.body" with this whsec_ secret). It is not the secret of any webhook Timon receives.
secret.once: Copy it now: it will not be shown again. If it is lost, give the webhook a new one.
secret.label: Secret (masked)
secret.copyFailed: Copy failed: the secret is shown here, selected — copy it by hand (Ctrl+C / ⌘C) before closing.

howto.github: GitHub: repository Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook. Payload URL: the address below, content type application/json, Secret: this one.
howto.gitlab: GitLab: Settings → Webhooks. URL: the address below, Secret token: this one. GitLab sends it as is, so a captured call can be replayed: prefer a signed scheme when the sender offers one.
howto.standard: Standard Webhooks (Svix, Clerk, Resend…): paste this signing secret (whsec_…) in the provider's endpoint settings.
howto.generic: Your own sender: send X-Timon-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Timon-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "timestamp.body" with this secret>. Calls older than 5 minutes are refused.
howto.none: No secret: this route only answers calls made on this machine.

editor.name: Name *
editor.tzHint: IANA name. Empty: the daemon's time zone.
editor.slugHint: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. It ends the address the sender calls.

authHint.github: X-Hub-Signature-256: HMAC of the body. The secret is generated on creation.
authHint.gitlab: X-Gitlab-Token: the secret itself, sent with every call.
authHint.standard: webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers, ±5 minutes.
authHint.none: No proof of origin: only calls made on this machine, straight to the daemon, are accepted.

editor.coalesceHint: A burst of calls about the same entity runs the actions once, after the quiet period; a burst that never calms down still runs once the ceiling is reached.
editor.noFilterForSchedule: A schedule receives no payload: there is nothing to filter. Go on to the actions.
editor.pathHint: Dotted paths into the payload: issue.title, commits.0.id; headers.X-GitHub-Event reads a header. "is one of" takes values separated by commas.
editor.filterIgnored: A call the filter turns down is answered "ignored" and logged, without running anything.
editor.templateHint: Insert a value of the payload with '{field.path}', e.g. '{issue.title}'.
editor.untrusted: Payload values are untrusted input: a task prompt receives them behind a warning, and the agent is chosen here, never by the payload.
editor.webhookHint: Timon POSTs '{type, timestamp, data}' here, data being the payload as received, signed with a secret shown once on save. Retried with back-off for up to 10 attempts. Everything the filter lets through leaves this machine.
editor.urgencyHint: Kept only if it renders to one of: {list}.
editor.agentHint: The agent that receives the task.
editor.rawPrompt: This prompt is sent as written, templates included.
editor.silentReturnHint: The agent's report stays where the task puts it (an idea's notes, a notification); its return never goes up to the orchestrator.
editor.workflowHint: Its published version runs; the payload becomes the run input.
editor.workflowNoEntry: This workflow has no entry node (manual, schedule, webhook or event) to start from.
editor.workflowsOff: The Workflows module is off: this action does nothing until it is switched back on.
editor.scriptNote: Runs a program on this machine, with no agent and no model: a tick costs no token. Only you can set this up — an agent never can.
editor.scriptCommandHint: A name on the PATH, an absolute path, or a path relative to the folder. No shell: to use one, write it out (bash, then -c and the line as arguments).
editor.scriptArgsHint: One per line, passed as they are. Nothing from a payload is ever inserted.
editor.scriptCwdHint: Absolute path inside a registered project. The program runs there.
editor.scriptEnvHint: Vault secret names, comma-separated (inject mode, granted globally or to this project). Their values never appear in the journal.
editor.scriptOverlap: Allow a run to start while the previous one is still going

telemetrySettings.title: Anonymous usage statistics
telemetrySettings.description: Timon can tell its team how the app is used — which features, how often turns succeed, where setup stops — so we know what to fix first. It is anonymous: a random identifier drawn on this computer, never your account or your machine.
telemetrySettings.shareDescription: On by default. Turning it off stops all sending right away; one last message records that you turned it off.
telemetrySettings.lockedEnv: Set by the TIMON_TELEMETRY environment variable: change it there.
telemetrySettings.lockedEnvMalformed: TIMON_TELEMETRY holds a value that is neither yes nor no: sharing is off.
telemetrySettings.lockedConfig: Set by telemetry.enabled in timon.config.json: change it there.
telemetrySettings.lockedConfigMalformed: telemetry.enabled in timon.config.json is neither true nor false: sharing is off.
telemetrySettings.inactiveBuild: This build of Timon sends nothing, whatever this setting says.
telemetrySettings.sent: App version, operating system, licence tier; app starts and updates; setup steps; turns, their duration, outcome and token counts; which built-in tools and providers are used; task, plugin, licence and browser actions as counts.
telemetrySettings.never: Your prompts, answers or files; names of your projects, agents, skills, routines or MCP servers; paths, URLs and commands; error messages; your email, user name, computer name or address.
telemetrySettings.forbidden: Only an administrator of this Timon can change this setting.
